history.heading: Ancient Vietnam and Chinese rule
paragraphs: Vietnam's Red River delta was home to the Dong Son culture, famous for bronze drums. According to legend, the Hùng kings founded the first Vietnamese state. China ruled northern Vietnam for about a thousand years, from 111 BCE to 938 CE, when Ngô Quyền won independence at the Battle of Bạch Đằng. Resistance heroes include the Trưng Sisters, who led a revolt in 40 CE.

history.heading: Dynasties
paragraphs: Independent dynasties, such as the Lý, Trần and Lê, ruled from Thăng Long (Hanoi) and repelled Mongol invasions in the 13th century. Vietnam expanded southward, absorbing the Cham kingdom of Champa and the Mekong Delta from the Khmer. The Nguyễn dynasty unified the country in 1802 with its capital at Huế.

history.heading: French rule and wars
paragraphs: France conquered Vietnam between 1858 and 1885, making it part of French Indochina. Hồ Chí Minh founded the Indochinese Communist Party and, after the Japanese occupation, declared independence on 2 September 1945. The First Indochina War ended with French defeat at Điện Biên Phủ in 1954, and Vietnam was divided into a communist North and an anti-communist South.

The Vietnam War followed, with the United States sending hundreds of thousands of troops to support the South. Millions of Vietnamese died. US forces withdrew in 1973, and northern forces captured Saigon on 30 April 1975, reunifying the country. Many people fled as "boat people". Vietnam invaded Cambodia in 1978 to oust the Khmer Rouge and fought a border war with China in 1979.

history.heading: Đổi Mới
paragraphs: In 1986 Vietnam launched Đổi Mới ("renovation") reforms, moving to a market economy under communist rule. Relations with the United States were normalised in 1995, and Vietnam joined the WTO in 2007. In 2025 the government carried out a major restructuring, merging provinces and cutting the size of the state.

culture.heading: Traditions
paragraphs: Vietnamese is the official language, written in a Latin-based script. Religion blends Buddhism, Confucianism, Taoism and ancestor worship, and there are Catholic and Cao Đài communities. Tết, the Lunar New Year, is the most important holiday.

Vietnamese cuisine is famous for phở (noodle soup), bánh mì, fresh spring rolls and coffee. Water puppetry is a traditional art. Hạ Long Bay and the ancient town of Hội An are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

politics.heading: One-party state
paragraphs: Vietnam is a one-party socialist republic led by the Communist Party of Vietnam, whose General Secretary is the most powerful figure. An anti-corruption campaign has led to the removal of senior leaders. Vietnam pursues a balanced foreign policy, with close ties to both the US and China, despite disputes with China in the South China Sea.

economy.heading: A manufacturing star
paragraphs: Vietnam has been one of the world's fastest-growing economies for decades, lifting millions out of poverty. It is a major manufacturing hub for electronics (Samsung makes many of its phones there), clothing, footwear and furniture, attracting companies diversifying away from China.
It is also a leading exporter of rice, coffee (the world's second-largest producer), cashews and seafood. The currency is the đồng.
